Critical perspectives / PAPER 12

Efficient at what, and for whom?

Why an AI-native organisation needs to count useful outcomes, the resources behind them and the relationships that let it operate.

ŁUKASZ STOCKI & ARGOPUBLIC EDITION / 05 NOV 20263 MIN READ
IN THIS PAPER
01 / Activity is an incomplete account02 / Give each attractive number an adversary03 / A test result has a boundary04 / Legitimacy is part of the operating environment↗ Open questions
EXPLORE THE LIBRARY ↗
WORKING PAPER · DESIGN & ANALYSIS
01

Activity is an incomplete account

An organisation can produce more messages, code and decisions while becoming less useful. It can also reduce the cost of one operation while increasing the cost of the whole task. Omnicorp’s measurement proposal begins with the outcome: what changed for someone, how was that change checked, and what did it consume?

Resources include computation, energy, elapsed time and human attention. Repair, review and incidents belong in the same account as generation. This is a design principle for future measurement, not a published result showing that Omnicorp has already achieved a particular level of efficiency.

02

Give each attractive number an adversary

Revenue per person can make a small organisation appear remarkably productive. Read alone, it can also reward removing people, outsourcing burdens or spending heavily on computation. Cost per task can improve while the task becomes less valuable. Completion rates can rise when difficult cases disappear from the denominator.

A more useful scoreboard pairs competing views. Throughput sits beside rework. Lower spending sits beside outcome quality. Autonomy sits beside escalation and recovery. Commercial performance sits beside the ability to explain decisions and address failures. The purpose of the pairing is to expose a tradeoff before a single favourable number conceals it.

03

A test result has a boundary

Checks help make claims inspectable, but a passed evaluation is evidence about its stated conditions. It does not establish competence across every neighbouring task or guarantee behaviour after deployment. Omnicorp’s later analysis explicitly challenges the temptation to turn a score into a general capability claim.

The practical response is to report coverage, preserve failures and examine outcomes beyond the test setting. The evaluator must be open to correction too. More tests are not automatically better if they repeat the same assumptions, and an increasingly elaborate dashboard can still be measuring the wrong thing.

04

Legitimacy is part of the operating environment

Usefulness does not cancel consent or responsibility. An organisation depends on people being willing to deal with it, understand its promises and obtain a response when those promises fail. Legal permission and public confidence are distinct questions; neither can be replaced by an internal claim of efficiency.

Our working position is that trust, quality and accountability can support durable performance together. That is an organisational argument, not a theorem that good conduct always wins. Competition can reward shortcuts, and feedback can arrive late. The response is to make those pressures visible and retain the ability to stop or redesign a harmful activity.

For a project whose purpose is continual development, measurement should help distinguish increased capability from increased motion. A simple relevance question remains valuable: if a particular activity stopped, who would lose something useful, and could we explain why?

THE NEXT QUESTIONS

What remains open.

  • Does the outcome remain useful after repair and review are counted?
  • What does each evaluation actually cover?
  • Who can challenge the organisation’s account of the value it creates?

ABOUT THIS EDITION

Adapted from the Omnicorp working document “10 EFFICIENCY AND LEGITIMACY”. This is an edited public essay, not a verbatim release of internal notes. The founding purpose is continual development of the organisation’s ability to understand and act; commercial and physical work sustain and ground it.
